learningObjectives: Use a noun-modifying clause as the subject, object or destination in a larger sentence.
Keep inner-clause particles separate from the particle after the described noun.
Describe when something happened with Nのとき or plain form + とき.
Complete a spoken information gap by asking for decisive descriptive details.
Read and hand-write 番 and 組 in 番組.

scene.where: A living-room sofa with a remote control balanced on one arm
scene.hook: Three programme cards are open, but the remote has only one confirm button.

lines.japanese: ぼくは ミクが 歌う 番組を 見たいです。
lines.reading: ぼくは ミクが うたう ばんぐみを みたいです。
lines.english: I want to watch the programme where Miku sings.
lines.note: The described noun phrase takes を in the main sentence.

lines.japanese: わたしは 字幕が 分かりやすい ドラマが いいです。
lines.reading: わたしは じまくが わかりやすい ドラマが いいです。
lines.english: I'd prefer a drama with easy-to-understand subtitles.
lines.note: The inner subject 字幕 takes が; the whole drama phrase also takes が outside.

lines.japanese: 子どもの ときに 見た アニメを もう 一度 見たいです。
lines.reading: こどもの ときに みた アニメを もう いちど みたいです。
lines.english: I want to rewatch an anime I saw as a child.
lines.note: A time phrase sits inside the clause that modifies アニメ.

lines.japanese: じゃあ、三人が 楽しめる 番組は どれですか。
lines.reading: じゃあ、さんにんが たのしめる ばんぐみは どれですか。
lines.english: Then which programme can all three of us enjoy?
lines.note: A potential-form clause identifies the head noun 番組.

lines.japanese: 条件が 三つ ありますね。長い 説明を 一つの 名詞に まとめましょう。
lines.reading: じょうけんが みっつ ありますね。ながい せつめいを ひとつの めいしに まとめましょう。
lines.english: We have three conditions. Let's gather each longer description around one noun.
lines.note: Rie names the structural task plainly.

explanation.recap: In l2plus-l07, a plain clause identified a person or item: 黒い帽子をかぶっている人. Now that whole described noun phrase will move through a larger sentence.
explanation.intro: The clause before a noun tells us which one; the particle after the noun tells us what that whole phrase does next. In 友達がすすめた番組を見ます, が belongs to the inner recommender and を belongs to the programme in the main sentence. Your clause can now do more than identify—it can carry a complete programme recommendation.

grammarPoints.nameJa: 説明した 名詞の 文での 役割
grammarPoints.meaning: the described noun as subject, object or place
grammarPoints.explanation: First close the description around the head noun, then add the particle required by the main sentence: ［友達がすすめた番組］を見ます; ［字幕が分かりやすい番組］が好きです; ［兄が働いている会社］へ行きます. Reading in chunks keeps the two layers clear.
grammarPoints.watchFor: The particle after the head noun belongs to the main sentence, not the modifier.
grammarPoints.commonError: Dropping the outer particle: 友達がすすめた番組見ます. The programme is the object, so add を.

examples.ja: ルパーナさんが すすめた 番組を 録画しました。
examples.reading: ルパーナさんが すすめた ばんぐみを ろくがしました。
examples.en: I recorded the programme Ruparna recommended.
examples.note: Inner が marks Ruparna; outer を marks the programme.

examples.ja: 外国で 作られた ドラマが 人気です。
examples.reading: がいこくで つくられた ドラマが にんきです。
examples.en: A drama made abroad is popular.
examples.note: The whole described phrase takes subject が.

examples.ja: 父が 働いている 会社へ 行きました。
examples.reading: ちちが はたらいて いる かいしゃへ いきました。
examples.en: I went to the company where my father works.
examples.note: The described place takes destination へ.

grammarPoints.nameJa: 二つの がを 読む
grammarPoints.meaning: an inner subject and an outer subject
grammarPoints.explanation: A sentence can legitimately contain two が particles at different layers: ［字幕が分かりやすいドラマ］が好きです. The first marks 字幕 as the thing that is easy to understand inside the description. The second marks the whole drama phrase as the thing liked. Bracket the head noun while checking.
grammarPoints.watchFor: Do not automatically delete one が; ask which clause each belongs to.
grammarPoints.commonError: Changing the inner が to を because two が look strange. 分かりやすい describes 字幕, so 字幕が is correct.

examples.ja: 音楽が きれいな 映画が 好きです。
examples.reading: おんがくが きれいな えいがが すきです。
examples.en: I like films whose music is beautiful.
examples.note: Inner 音楽が; outer 映画が.

examples.ja: 主人公が 強い ドラマが 始まります。
examples.reading: しゅじんこうが つよい ドラマが はじまります。
examples.en: A drama with a strong protagonist is starting.
examples.note: Two layers, two valid が particles.

grammarPoints.pattern: Nの とき / plain form + とき
grammarPoints.explanation: A noun takes の before とき: 子どものとき. A verb or い-adjective uses its plain form: 見るとき, 見たとき, 忙しいとき. A な-adjective takes な: ひまなとき. This time phrase can sit inside a larger modifier: 子どものときに見た番組.
grammarPoints.watchFor: The form before とき matches its word type; the verb tense shows whether the action is complete relative to that moment.
grammarPoints.commonError: Saying 子どもとき or ひまだとき. Use 子どものとき and ひまなとき.

examples.ja: 子どもの ときに 見た 番組です。
examples.reading: こどもの ときに みた ばんぐみです。
examples.en: It is a programme I watched as a child.

examples.ja: ひまな ときに 録画した ドラマを 見ます。
examples.reading: ひまな ときに ろくがした ドラマを みます。
examples.en: When I am free, I watch dramas I recorded.

examples.ja: 家を 出る とき、テレビを 消します。
examples.reading: いえを でる とき、テレビを けします。
examples.en: I turn off the television when leaving home.
examples.note: Non-past 出る means before or as leaving.

mission.title: The programme information gap
mission.prompt: Two people hold incomplete descriptions of four fictional programmes. Ask only spoken questions, fill every missing field, and agree on the one programme that meets three audience conditions.
successCriteria: You ask at least four questions built around noun-modifying clauses.
You recover who appears, what the programme introduces, and who recorded it.
You correctly use an inner subject が and an outer particle in one answer.
You identify one programme satisfying all three conditions.
You justify the choice with three complete descriptive noun phrases.

modelAnswer.ja: 選んだのは 「町の 台所」です。小さい 店で 働く 人が 出る 番組です。町の 料理を 紹介する 番組で、ルパーナさんが 録画した 番組です。字幕が 読みやすい 番組が 好きな 人にも 合います。
modelAnswer.reading: えらんだのは 「まちの だいどころ」です。ちいさい みせで はたらく ひとが でる ばんぐみです。まちの りょうりを しょうかいする ばんぐみで、ルパーナさんが ろくがした ばんぐみです。じまくが よみやすい ばんぐみが すきな ひとにも あいます。
modelAnswer.en: We chose Town Kitchens. It is a programme featuring people who work in small shops. It introduces local cooking and is the programme Ruparna recorded. It also suits people who like programmes with readable subtitles.

instruction.form: plain clause + noun / Nのとき / plain form + とき
instruction.meaning: add detail about a noun and place an event in time
instruction.commonContrast: the inner subject of a noun-modifying clause often uses が; とき gives a time frame, not an automatic result

workedExamples.en: An original Yomu context model; use it to notice the target before creating your own response.

guidedPractice.prompt: First find the target in context. Then make a parallel attempt from a cue; the completed response remains hidden until after the attempt.

progressiveHints.text: Choose one situation where you would naturally use plain clause + noun / Nのとき / plain form + とき; do not write the whole sentence yet.
Build the sentence in parts: choose the content first, then check the form that carries add detail about a noun and place an event in time.
Compare your form, meaning, and neutral explanation with the worked model. Change the content so the response is your own.

retryFeedback.diagnostic: Check the form and meaning again. A common mix-up is this: the inner subject of a noun-modifying clause often uses が; とき gives a time frame, not an automatic result
